messages:
jamie: FYI: saw a ~8% tail CPU increase on host-proxy after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. quick flame link: https://flame.internal/8912345679
ravi: which tweak exactly? the small-seq fastpath change?
jamie: yeah — we flipped default to 'fastpath' kernels for seqs < 64 to hit lower latency. but profiler shows more syscall churn on ingress (lots of tiny writes).
maria: can you paste perf snapshot?
jamie: ```
# perf top (sample)
25.6%  host_parser::process_frame
18.2%  syscall_write
12.4%  grpc::ServerRead
8.9%   tokenizer::tokenize
6.3%   kv_cache::get
...
```
sami: syscall_write spikes usually mean many small socket writes — suggests we're not coalescing frames or writev use is missing.
kevin: also possible batching heuristics are causing premature flush (mini-batches of 1). combo of early kernel fastpath + tiny writes = overhead.
lina: KV cache telemetry shows higher miss amplification: fragmented keys from prefix-slicing. prefetch entropy went up when fastpath used.
jamie: repro steps: run canary traffic profile `ingress/smallwrite-500rps-32toks` against canary build 2026-03-18T22:10. saw p50 +7% and p95 +10% on host-proxy CPU.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy complete: build 2026-03-18T22:10 -> canary cluster (ID: can-21)
maria: quick experiment idea: change kernel selection policy to prefer 'packed' kernels when avg_seq < 64 AND pending_incoming > 4 (so we avoid fastpath when there's ingress pressure).
ravi: agree. another quick win: buffer small frames up to 2KB before parsing to reduce small-write echoes — defer parsing until we have a full first-chunk or timer fires.
kevin: i ran a local sandbox with writev coalescing fallback: reduced syscall count by ~70% and host_parser CPU down ~4%.
jamie: nice — can you share the minimal patch?
kevin: ```c
// pseudo diff
ssize_t maybe_writev(int fd, const struct iovec *iov, int iovcnt) {
  // coalesce small iovs into a stack buffer up to 8KB, otherwise call writev
}
```
maria: after applying writev + kernel-policy tweak in sandbox: p95 dropped ~6%, kv-miss-rate down 2.3%, and overall tail CPU normalized.
sami: rollout proposal: land writev fallback + kernel policy in canary, monitor 24h; if stable -> 1% prod -> 10% -> ramp. rollback if p50 regresses >2% or error rate climbs.
jamie: follow-ups: @kevin open PR with writev fallback (ENG-RT PR), @maria bench kernel-selection heuristic and publish perf matrix (ENG-RT-211), @ravi investigate tokenization placement + KV prefetch tweaks (ENG-RT-212).
kevin: will open PR today and add unit + perf test. :thumbsup:
jamie: thanks — assigning and adding notes to the incident board. I'll attach flamegraph + perf artifacts to ENG-RT ticket.
lina: one more note — streaming chunking timer currently set to 10ms; maybe increase to 15ms for high-ingress modes to allow coalescing without hurting latency too much. worth A/B.
maria: good call. adding experiment to the bench matrix.
jamie: ok everyone, let's converge on PR + canary run tomorrow morning. thanks for the quick triage.
